widget.caption: Change the lengths and the angle θ (radians). The curve shows a·b over θ from 0 to π.

variants.why: Parallel vectors (θ = 0) would give 0, and perpendicular vectors would give the maximum. The dot product must be largest when the vectors point the same way.
The sign is lost. Opposite vectors (θ = π) would give +6 instead of −6, so anti-correlated series would look like correlated ones.

params.name: a
params.effect: longer a: the dot product grows in proportion

params.name: b
params.effect: longer b: the dot product grows in proportion

params.name: t
params.effect: larger angle: the dot product falls, is 0 at 90°, and is negative after that

widget.caption: Set the two components of v. The curve shows the length as x changes, with y fixed.

parts.label: square root: back to data units

variants.why: Without the root, (3, 4) gets 25, not 5, and doubling the vector makes the 'length' 4 times larger. A length must scale by the same factor as the vector.
(3, 4) gets about 2.92, not 5. The components are squared, so only the square root undoes it and matches Pythagoras.

checks.label: (−3, 4): the sign does not change the length

widget.caption: Here a = (2, 1) and b = (1, 2). Scale a by k. The dot product grows, but the cosine stays at 0.8.

parts.label: product of lengths: cancels the scale

variants.why: The scale of a is not removed. The value grows with k and passes 1, so it is no longer a cosine.
Squared lengths over-correct. The value falls as k grows, so the same shape gets different scores at different scales.
A sum does not cancel a product. The value changes with k, so the score depends on the units of the series.

params.name: k
params.effect: larger k: a gets longer, but the cosine stays 0.8

checks.label: k = 4: still 0.8; scale does not matter

widget.caption: Majority vote of 3 independent agents. Move p and try other coefficients.

parts.label: number of ways to pick the dissenter

variants.why: Counts only one of the three orders of who is wrong. At p = 0.5 the vote gives 0.25, worse than one coin-flip agent, which is wrong by symmetry.
Misses one arrangement. At p = 0.5 the result is 0.375, not 0.5, so the formula breaks the symmetry between right and wrong.
Overcounts arrangements. At p = 0.5 it gives 0.875, and at p = 0.9 it gives more than 1, which is not a probability.

params.name: p
params.effect: larger p: each agent is more accurate and the vote gains even more

checks.label: coin-flip agents give a coin-flip vote
perfect agents give a perfect vote
p = 0.7 gives 0.784, better than one agent

widget.caption: Expected cost of a 2-stage cascade, small model cost = 1. Move the acceptance rate a and the large-model cost r.

variants.why: Forgets that the small model runs on every query. The cascade then never costs more than the large model, which hides the real overhead at a = 0.

parts.label: fraction escalated to the large model

variants.why: Pays the large model on accepted queries instead of rejected ones. Cost would rise as the small model gets better, which is backwards.
There is no reason to square the escalation rate; each rejected query calls the large model exactly once.

params.name: a
params.effect: larger a: more queries stop at the small model, cost falls

params.name: r
params.effect: larger r: escalation is more expensive, a good scorer matters more

checks.label: all escalated: costs more than the large model (10)
all accepted: only the small model's cost

widget.caption: Compute of a swap run (T = 1, prefill ignored). Change model sizes and the swap point s.

parts.label: model A writes the first part

variants.why: Charges B for A's share of tokens. At s = 0 (B writes everything) B would cost nothing, which is wrong.
Charges B for the whole output even when A wrote part of it. The swap point then has no effect on B's cost.

params.name: s
params.effect: larger s: A writes more of the output

params.name: na
params.effect: larger N_A: each token of A costs more

params.name: nb
params.effect: larger N_B: each token of B costs more

widget.caption: Two-token soft message: weight on token 1. Change the logit gap and the temperature.

parts.label: logit gap between the two tokens
temperature: how soft the message is

params.name: d
params.effect: larger gap: the message moves toward token 1's embedding

params.name: t
params.effect: larger T: the message becomes a more even mix of both tokens

checks.label: equal logits give an even mix
